eval_independent/16_global_temperature_g.name: Global temperature annual versus monthly aggregation (negative control)

Source.explanation: Both resource dictionaries define the same data-provider identifier. The archived converter assigns GISTEMP to NASA rows and GCAG to HadCRUT rows in both annual and monthly outputs. This identifies the provider, not the observation period.

Year.explanation: The complete annual schema identifies YYYY calendar years; the complete monthly schema identifies YYYY-MM calendar months. Its Source and Mean fields are not years either. Under the existing protocol a full calendar coordinate is not equivalent to a component: extracting a year from a month or changing observation granularity requires a transformation.

Mean.explanation: The annual Mean is an annual average temperature anomaly; the monthly Mean is the anomaly for a specific month. They share a name and unit but have different aggregation periods, expressly excluded as direct equivalents by the frozen annotation policy. Source and Year are identifiers, not annual means.

eval_independent/16_global_temperature_g.role: new held-out negative control; no predictions inspected before freeze
eval_independent/16_global_temperature_g.provenance_limitation: The publisher README retains stale NOAA/GCAG wording and its dictionary retains a 20th-century baseline description; the pinned processing script and source URLs identify the GCAG-labelled data as HadCRUT5.1.0.0. We archive these inconsistencies unchanged, do not claim direct agency retrieval, and use only documented identifiers and aggregation periods as label evidence.
